Confirmed: the diagnosis matches. `spawnSync` defaults to a 1 MB `maxBuffer`, and this PR's diff (41k+ files touched, likely from an unrelated-history merge) produces a `--name-only` list bigger than that. When the buffer overflows, Node sets `result.error` (ENOBUFS), `status` becomes `null`, and `stderr` stays an empty string — exactly the silent `git diff failed: ` with no message seen in the log.

All covered. Let's verify the file compiles cleanly.

The root cause: `git diff --name-only main...HEAD` in `check-changeset-coverage.ts` was run via `spawnSync` with the default 1 MB `maxBuffer`. This PR's diff touches 40k+ files, so the output overflowed the buffer — Node aborts with `ENOBUFS` (`status: null`, empty `stderr`), which the script logged as the unhelpful `git diff failed: ` with no message.

Fix: bumped `maxBuffer` to 64 MB on the `git diff`, `git merge-base`, and `git show` calls in [check-changeset-coverage.ts](scripts/release/check-changeset-coverage.ts#L103-L134), and surfaced `result.error` explicitly so a future buffer overflow (or other spawn failure) produces a real message instead of a blank one.
